grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.slogan: Austria's showpiece toll road to a glacier viewpoint at 2500 m.
grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.story: The Grossglockner road was built to be ridden slowly and looked at: thirty-six hairpins, a museum at the top and the Pasterze glacier at the end of the Franz-Josefs-Höhe spur. It is a toll road with published opening hours, and the gates close overnight - a late start can leave you locked out.

waypoints.name: Bruck an der Glocknerstrasse
waypoints.advice: Bruck an der Glocknerstrasse is where the day begins. Next is Fuscher Törl, climbing 1671 m.

waypoints.name: Fuscher Törl
waypoints.advice: You top out at 2428 m here. The road climbs 1671 m over at least 19 km before it, steeply. Reckon on about 11 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Hochtor.

waypoints.name: Hochtor
waypoints.advice: 2504 m, and the road stops climbing. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Franz-Josefs-Höhe.

waypoints.name: Franz-Josefs-Höhe
waypoints.advice: Franz-Josefs-Höhe, about halfway at 2369 m. Reckon on about 10 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Heiligenblut, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Heiligenblut
waypoints.advice: Heiligenblut is the finish, 48 km from Bruck. The descent from Hochtor drops about 1,068 m in a series of long, open hairpins - take it on engine braking rather than the brakes, and expect cyclists and coaches on the inside line.

grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.speedBand: Posted limits vary by country - read the signs, not the app

sections.advice: The northern ramp: through Fusch to the toll station at Ferleiten, then the climb begins in earnest through the numbered hairpins towards Fuscher Törl. Set a rhythm early; the bends keep coming.
sections.source: Sections written 2026-10-03 from the route's own stops; facts from Austria Tourism (austria.info). Leg distances not measured, so none is stated.

sections.advice: Along the high section to the Hochtor at 2,504 m, where Salzburg meets Carinthia and the road passes through the summit tunnel. Expect cold air and wind at the top whatever the valley said.
sections.source: Sections written 2026-10-03 from the route's own stops; facts from Austria Tourism (austria.info). Leg distances not measured, so none is stated.

sections.advice: Down the southern side and along the spur to the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe, the viewpoint over the Grossglockner and the Pasterze glacier. It is a dead end: you ride back the same way to rejoin the road.
sections.source: Sections written 2026-10-03 from the route's own stops; facts from Austria Tourism (austria.info). Leg distances not measured, so none is stated.

sections.advice: Back along the spur and down to Heiligenblut. A long descent on a toll road that is normally open from early May to early November; brakes and gearing matter more than speed here.
sections.source: Sections written 2026-10-03 from the route's own stops; facts from Austria Tourism (austria.info). Leg distances not measured, so none is stated.

scenicChapters.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2428 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Grossglockner Hochalpenstrasse
scenicChapters.narrative: 37 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.
